items: Write the recipe card for the dish: every ingredient, by brand and product, in the amounts you use.
For each thing you buy, photograph the front of the package and the ingredient list. If it comes in a case with no retail label, ask the sup
Read every label down to the sub-ingredients (what is inside the sauce, the bread, the spice blend).
Take out anything with honey, beeswax, carmine (also called cochineal or E120), shellac (confectioner's glaze), gelatin, isinglass or animal
For these ten, ask the maker in writing and keep the answer: natural flavors, wine, beer, vinegar, vitamin D3, cane sugar, enzymes, glycerin
"May contain milk" or a shared-facility line is not a fail. Note it; it goes in the dish's disclosure.

items: Walk the dish from the shelf to the plate and write down every base it uses: stock, dough, bread or bun, glaze, sauce, dressing, marinade, p

If a base is shared with other dishes (a house sauce, a pizza dough), it must pass for this dish too, or this dish gets its own.

items: Storage: give the dish's ingredients their own shelf or bin, labeled, never under raw animal products unless covered.
Tools: set aside a pan, pot, tongs, ladle and cutting board for the dish (a color you use for nothing else works well). Or use a pan that is
Surfaces: a clean sheet, foil or a dedicated tray between the dish and any shared surface.
Fryer: a dedicated fryer, or no frying for this dish. Shared oil with chicken or fish is a fail, no matter how often it is changed.
Water: fresh water for pasta or vegetables, never the pot that cooked anything else.
Grill or flat-top: scrape and clean it before the dish goes on, every time, or use a barrier or a separate pan on top.
Oven: covered or on its own tray, and write down how you do it. Send that procedure with your evidence.
Garnish: a separate garnish container for the dish, not the shared station with cheese, butter or bacon.
Dedicated pan, pot, utensils and board
A shared pan, cleaned and sanitized, used only for this dish during its cook
A clean barrier on a shared surface
Shared oven, covered or on its own tray, under a written procedure
Shared fryer oil with any animal product
Pasta or vegetable water shared with animal products
A grill used for meat and not cleaned first
Tongs or ladles moving between the dish and animal products
A shared garnish station with no separation

items: List every place the dish appears: printed menu, boards, website, QR menu, each delivery app, your social accounts.
Use the same dish name everywhere, word for word.
Put the mark only next to certified dishes, with the menu key ("Plant-Based Dish, Pre-Vegan Certified") on the same page or screen.
Never call the restaurant Vegan, never put the mark on the door or the whole menu, never write "Vegan" alone on a certified dish, and never
On delivery apps, ask each platform to change a dish called "Vegan" to the certified name with the key in the description.
